findings.passage: HB 4145 infringes on constitutional rights, burdens law enforcement without support, and fails to deliver measurable public safety improvements. I urge the committee to reject this bill.
findings.note: Her written testimony to House Judiciary against HB 4145 (permit to buy a firearm, higher fee, longer wait, 10-round magazine limit).

findings.passage: HB 4145 raises the permit fee from $65 to $150—more than doubling the cost for law-abiding citizens. It extends issuance timelines from 30 to 60 days, creating lengthy delays in exercising constitutional rights.
findings.note: Objects to the higher permit fee and the 60-day permit wait in HB 4145.

findings.passage: No Public Safety Gains. Most critically, this system does nothing to address the real drivers of gun violence: straw purchasing, criminal trafficking, stolen firearms, domestic violence enforcement, suicide prevention, and mental health intervention.
findings.note: Says the permit system does not address what she names as the causes of gun violence.

findings.passage: What occurred in committee surrounding this bill should concern every member of this chamber—regardless of party or position on the policy itself,
findings.note: Quote in a House caucus release on HB 4145; she speaks about how the committee vote was handled, not about the gun policy itself.

findings.passage: I write to oppose both House Bill 3075 and 3076. Oregon already has some of the strictest gun laws in the nation. This Legislature should focus on enforcing those laws instead of passing new ones.
findings.note: Written testimony opposing HB 3075 (Measure 114 permit changes) and HB 3076 (gun dealer rules).

findings.passage: Additional regulations would not enhance public safety but would instead harm small businesses and limit the rights of lawful gun owners.
findings.note: Objects to added rules on licensed gun dealers in HB 3076.

findings.passage: It is currently legal under Oregon and Federal law for a person to make an unserialized firearm themselves for their own use as long as they do not sell or otherwise transfer it. This bill would instantly criminalize thousands of Oregonians who possess these firearms.
findings.note: Written testimony against HB 2005 (unserialised home-made guns).

findings.passage: We should not be deciding who gets to exercise their constitutional rights, like the 2nd Amendment, and who doesn’t.
findings.note: Against HB 2006, which would bar 18-to-20-year-olds from having a rifle.
subjects: minimum age to own a rifle

findings.passage: Everyone should be able to protect themselves, even if they don’t have the State Police protecting them.
findings.note: Against HB 2007, which widens where guns are barred (public buildings and adjacent ground), arguing it undercuts concealed handgun licences.

findings.passage: This is the biggest threat to Oregonian's Second Amendment Rights in recent memory.
findings.note: Her district newsletter on HB 3075 (permit class, 10-round magazine limit, Measure 114 changes), with a call to testify.
